cells.rationale: Official Treasury par curve (source of DGS10) shows 10y at 5.28 on 2026-10-02 (5.24 on 10-01; 5.29 peak 09-30). One CNBC headline summary claimed 5.18 after the payrolls miss, conflicting with the official print; I weight the official 5.28 ~90%. Starting 4bp above threshold, with ~5bp daily vol (20d realized 5.2bp) over 1 trading day(s), a random walk gives ~0.71; shaded down for the conflicting report and for mean-reversion risk after the weak September payrolls cut October hike odds to ~17-21%. Probability decays with horizon. Confidence: medium; a single-day move of 4bp or more is common, so this is close to a coin flip with a positive tilt.

The last three first prints were 198k, 198k and 197k (4-week average 200k; consensus last week was 200k). The threshold sits right at the current level, and a 197k print resolves NO. Layoffs remain low, while payroll growth is weak. The hurricane season is historically quiet, so there is no storm distortion. Week-to-week first-print sd is about 8k, so the probability is roughly even, with a slight upward tilt toward the 4-week average offset by the downward trend. Confidence: low-medium; essentially a coin flip.
